This study examines whether cloud optical thickness (COT), retrieved from the same imagery under cloud-product supervision, improves global horizontal irradiance (GHI) estimation and remains useful in short-term forecasting. A frozen retriever supplies spatially aligned local COT fields to a compact irradiance model alongside AGRI channels and solar geometry. Paired experiments use Hubei as the primary study region and Hunan as a complementary region. We examine overall estimation accuracy, dependence on cloud optical thickness, and continuous cloud events. The framework is then applied to forecast imagery over 15--240 min. after: Cloud optical thickness (COT) characterizes the attenuation of solar radiation by clouds. This study investigates whether including retrieved COT improves global horizontal irradiance (GHI) estimation when multispectral satellite imagery is already available. A retrieval model trained using satellite cloud products generates local COT fields, which are combined with AGRI imagery and solar geometry to estimate 15-minute mean GHI. Models with and without COT are compared at three stations in Hubei and two in Hunan, with separate training for each region. We evaluate overall errors and their dependence on cloud optical thickness, and examine cloud-passage and growth--dissipation events. We then apply the irradiance models to cloud images predicted 15--240 minutes ahead. Controlled input substitutions assess how errors in these images affect retrieved COT and GHI forecasts. \pending{Regional RMSEs with and without COT, relative reductions, and the main difference between cloud conditions.} \pending{Forecasting results and the measured contribution of cloud-image prediction errors.} The analysis examines when COT improves irradiance estimates and how cloud-image prediction errors affect this improvement in forecasting.

before: COT provides a physically defined coordinate for cloud attenuation within a learned irradiance mapping. Its contribution is practical if cloud-product supervision makes relevant information easier for a compact GHI model to use. This interpretation does not require COT to be an independent observation or the only useful representation. Capacity and retrieval-feature comparisons clarify how much of the measured benefit is shared with a richer representation of the same imagery.
after: COT describes optical attenuation by clouds and provides a physically interpretable input to the irradiance model. Training the retrieval model against cloud products may help the irradiance model use cloud information that is implicit in the spectral inputs. Comparisons with additional image features and retrieval-model features assess how much of the improvement is associated with increased model capacity or cloud-property supervision.

before: COT在学习得到的辐照度映射中提供了有明确物理定义的云衰减表征。若云产品监督使紧凑GHI模型更容易利用相关信息，其贡献就具有实际价值。这不要求COT是独立观测，也不要求它是唯一有效的表示。容量和反演器隐特征对照说明收益有多少可以由同源图像的更丰富表示共同解释。
after: COT描述云的光学衰减特征，为辐照度模型提供具有明确物理意义的输入。通过云产品训练反演模型，可能帮助辐照度模型利用光谱输入中隐含的云信息。与额外图像特征及反演模型特征的比较，用于评价模型容量增加和云属性监督分别与改善有多大关系。

before: The forecasting chain exposes two routes by which errors in extrapolated imagery can affect GHI. One changes the spectral and spatial input to the irradiance model directly. The other changes the COT inferred from that same imagery. Cloud displacement can shift the inferred attenuation away from the station or to the wrong target time. Spatial smoothing can weaken cloud boundaries, and errors in cloud growth or dissipation can suppress or delay changes in retrieved optical thickness. Consequently, an effective COT representation in observed imagery need not retain the same benefit when supplied with extrapolated fields.
after: Errors in predicted cloud images can affect GHI directly through the spectral and spatial inputs and indirectly through the COT retrieved from those images. Errors in cloud position can change the location and timing of attenuation at the station. Spatial smoothing can reduce local COT contrasts, while errors in cloud growth and dissipation can suppress or delay changes in optical thickness. If the COT-related improvement is smaller with forecast imagery, these processes could help explain the reduction.

before: 底图外推误差可以通过两条路径影响GHI：一条直接改变辐照度模型接收的光谱和空间输入，另一条改变由同一预测图反演出的COT。云团位移可能使衰减信号偏离站点或出现在错误时刻；空间平滑可能削弱云边界；云团增长和消散误差可能压低或延迟光学厚度变化。因此，在真实云图中有效的COT表示，进入预测云场后未必保留相同程度的增益。
after: 云图预测误差既可以通过光谱和空间输入直接影响GHI，也可以通过这些图像反演出的COT间接影响GHI。云位置误差可能改变云衰减的空间位置和到站时刻；空间平滑可能削弱COT的局地对比；云团增长与消散误差则可能压低或延迟光学厚度变化。若预测云图条件下加入COT的改善幅度较小，这些过程可为该变化提供可能解释。

before: This analysis motivates a distinct next step: improving cloud-image forecasts so that they preserve the location, boundaries, and optical evolution relevant to irradiance. An appropriate future test would hold the retriever and irradiance mapping fixed while improving the upstream image prediction, and evaluate whether better cloud evolution translates into larger GHI gains. The present study establishes the role of COT and examines its sensitivity to forecast inputs; the subsequent study can address how to reduce those upstream errors.
after: Improving the prediction of cloud position, boundaries, and optical-thickness evolution is therefore a direction for further research. Holding the retrieval and irradiance models fixed would allow future work to test whether more accurate cloud-image predictions lead to further reductions in GHI forecast error.

after: 因此，改进云位置、边界及光学厚度演变的预测，是值得进一步研究的方向。后续可保持反演与辐照度模型不变，检验更准确的云图预测能否进一步降低GHI预报误差。
